Personal Training for Beginners and Anyone Nervous About Gyms

A private studio in Lakeview, not a gym. Your first 30-minute session is free.

Book your free first session

Transform Personal Training is a private, appointment-only personal training studio at 2900 N Broadway in Lakeview, Chicago. It isn't a gym. There's no membership, no crowd and nobody waiting for your bench. Most of the week it's just you and your trainer in a room of your own. Sessions are 30 minutes, and your first one is free.

This is for you if

  • You've never worked with a trainer, or you've never really exercised.
  • Gym intimidation has kept you from starting: the crowds, the mirrors, the feeling of being watched.
  • You're coming back after years off, an injury or a big life change.
  • You're older and want to get stronger safely.
  • You'd rather start with a friend or partner than on your own.

A studio, not a gym

Our studio has two connected training rooms. Most of the week there's one trainer working with one client, or two trainers who each have a room with their own client. Only for about 2 to 4 hours a week do three trainers and their clients share the space.

So no one is lifting next to you, no one is waiting for your equipment, and no one is watching. Ask any question, try something twice, or take a breather without feeling on display.

How getting started works

  1. 1

    A quick call with Dave.

    Dave Bostik, Transform's owner, calls you for 5 to 10 minutes. You talk about your goals, what you've done before, any injuries or limits, and when you can train. Then he books your free first session with the coach who fits you best.

  2. 2

    Your free first session.

    It's mostly a conversation. Your coach goes deeper on your goals and history and helps you work out a schedule. If you'd like, they can walk you through a quick, easy assessment. If you'd rather not, you won't do one.

  3. 3

    Start when you're ready.

    Most people decide to start at that first session, because our prices are already on the website and nothing is hidden. Training is month to month, with no long contracts and no big packages to buy.

What to bring

Workout clothes, a water bottle and any questions you have. That's it.

Why 30 minutes is a good way to start

Thirty minutes is long enough to learn the basics properly and short enough that it never feels like an ordeal. Your coach is with you the whole time, so you're never left wandering around wondering what to do next.

30-Minute vs 60-Minute Personal Training →

Choosing a coach

Tell Dave on your call what you're nervous about, and he'll match you with the right coach.

Miriam Plotkin has trained clients since 2001 and trained in comedy at Second City and iO. She keeps sessions fun, which helps if you're worried training will feel like punishment.

Gerri Bushkovski is a Corrective Exercise Specialist, certified in Pilates Reformer, pre- and post-natal training, and Apex Nutrition.

Eric-Todd Rushing spent 25 years as a professional dancer and is a certified professional coach (iPEC). He focuses on how you move and on getting past the mental side of starting.

Bring a friend

If you'd feel better starting with someone you know, our Group Max 3 option lets you train together with a friend, roommate or partner, up to three people. There are no preset classes or group times, and we never put you with strangers. Group sessions are $32.50 to $42.50 per person, depending on how often you train.

Price and hours

  • One-on-one: $55 a session at twice a week, $50 at three times, $45 at four times. Every session is 30 minutes.
  • Hours: by appointment, Monday to Thursday 5am to 9pm, Friday 5am to 8pm, Saturday 7am to 3pm.
  • First session: free.

See every plan on our studio services page, or compare with what a personal trainer costs in Chicago.

Why Transform works this way

Dave weighed 346 pounds when he started training in 2003 and lost 150 pounds working with a personal trainer, so he knows firsthand what starting feels like. He opened Transform to be a supportive, non-judgmental place where people feel comfortable getting started.

Questions beginners ask

Do I need to be in shape before I start?

No. Your coach builds every session around what you can do today, and you progress from there.

Will other people be watching me?

Almost never. We have two connected training rooms, and most of the week each trainer has a room with their client. Only for a few hours a week do three trainers share the space.

Will the first session be hard?

No. It's mostly a conversation. A quick assessment is optional, and only if you want one.

What should I wear or bring?

Workout clothes, a water bottle and your questions.

Is the first session really free? Will I be pressured to sign up?

Yes, it's free. Our prices are on the website, and training is month to month with no long contracts or big packages, so there's nothing to push.

How often should a beginner train?

Our plans are two, three or four 30-minute sessions a week. Your coach will help you choose what fits your schedule and goals.

Can I bring a friend?

Yes. Group Max 3 lets you train with up to two people you know. We never put you with strangers.

I'm older or have an old injury. Is that OK?

Yes. All of our trainers can work with seniors and people recovering from injuries. Tell Dave about any injuries on your first call, and he'll match you with the right coach. If your doctor has limited your exercise, check with them before you start.

Ready to start?
